content.text: Recursion is when a function calls itself to solve a problem by breaking it into smaller versions of the same problem. Each recursive call works on a simpler case until it reaches a "base case"—a simple version that can be solved directly without recursing further. The base case stops the function from calling itself infinitely; without it, the recursion would never end. A classic example is calculating factorial: to find 5!, you calculate 5 × 4!, which calculates 4 × 3!, and so on, until you reach 1! which equals 1 (the base case).
